official_measurement_examples.name: Official safeguarding maps
official_measurement_examples.fact: The DfT safeguarding direction uses site-specific colour-coded safeguarding maps to identify development types on which local planning authorities must consult the relevant aerodrome or technical-site consultee.

official_measurement_examples.name: OLS three-dimensional scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: CAA guidance describes Obstacle Limitation Surfaces as three-dimensional protected airspace around aerodromes; a simple planar radius or distance is not a height clearance decision.

official_measurement_examples.name: IFP separate assessment
official_measurement_examples.fact: CAA states Instrument Flight Procedures can extend beyond or be more restrictive than OLS in places and may need a separate assessment by an approved procedure design organisation.

official_measurement_examples.name: Wildlife safeguarding
official_measurement_examples.fact: Official safeguarding can include a 13km wildlife consultation circle for developments capable of increasing bird-strike risk; the circle is a consultation trigger rather than automatic refusal.

official_measurement_examples.name: Crane current notification
official_measurement_examples.fact: CAA guidance requires crane notification within 6km where height criteria are met or at 100m AGL regardless of location, and the ACOMS portal was launched 22 July 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2030 OLS transition
official_measurement_examples.fact: CAA's new ICAO OLS framework becomes globally applicable on 21 November 2030, so the future framework must not be represented as the current 2026 safeguarding surface.

official_measurement_examples.name: Wind turbine aviation
official_measurement_examples.fact: CAP 764 requires case-specific consideration of wind-turbine impacts on aviation systems; a 30km consultation map is not a universal exclusion zone.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Aerodrome consultation, obstacle notification, aerodrome safeguarding assessment and planning permission are distinct processes and none alone establishes parcel development capacity.

core_rules: a safeguarding consultation map is not planning refusal
distance from an aerodrome is not a three-dimensional obstacle clearance
OLS assessment is distinct from Instrument Flight Procedure safeguarding
CNS radar and navigation impacts must not be inferred from building height alone
a 13km wildlife consultation circle is not a universal development exclusion zone
a 30km wind-turbine consultation circle is not automatic refusal
crane notification is not planning permission
aerodrome operator consultation is not land ownership or access authority
future 2030 ICAO OLS must not be used as current 2026 legal geometry
current safeguarding maps may vary between aerodromes and must retain map-specific criteria
an aerodrome safeguarding response does not determine all other planning matters
CAP guidance does not create parcel development rights
aviation obstacle data does not determine title or private rights
aviation safety clearance does not reserve infrastructure or housing capacity
no parcel aviation clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official DfT/GOV.UK and UK CAA sources checked on 2026-07-26. Current safeguarding, July 2026 ACOMS crane notification and the future 2030 ICAO OLS transition were kept distinct; no parcel aviation clearance was promoted.
